evals.prompt: Run a CI security audit on the GitHub Actions workflows in evals/files/inject/.
evals.expected_output: ci-secure scans the workflow and reports a template-injection finding (P14.10) for the untrusted ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} expression used in a run: block, with a plain-English attacker scenario. A markdown report is produced only on the user's save pick. Nothing is committed or pushed.
expectations: The skill ran scripts/run.py (or scan.py) rather than eyeballing the YAML.
The findings include P14.10 with the exact workflow file and line.
Every rendered finding carries a 'What an attacker could do' scenario.
The report includes the scope-honesty line (critical exploit-chain checks only).
No git commit, push, or PR was created.

evals.prompt: Run a CI security audit on the GitHub Actions workflows in evals/files/clean/.
evals.expected_output: ci-secure scans and finds ZERO critical attack vectors. It says so plainly and positively — zero findings is a first-class result, not an error — while stating the scope honestly (critical-only, not a comprehensive audit) and reporting whether the network-gated impostor-SHA check ran or was skipped.
expectations: The skill reports zero findings without hedging or apologizing.
The scope-honesty line is present (this is not a comprehensive audit).
The impostor-SHA check's ran/skipped status is stated explicitly.
The skill does NOT invent lower-severity observations to fill space.

evals.prompt: Check evals/files/pwn-request/ for GitHub Actions security problems.
evals.expected_output: ci-secure reports P14.9 (fork code executed with privileges) on vulnerable.yml — pull_request_target + checkout of the PR head + execution — and reports NOTHING on safe.yml, which runs the same build under plain pull_request. The fix recipe recommends the pull_request trigger split.
expectations: safe.yml is scanned and produces no finding (the negative is real, not a coverage gap).
The attacker scenario names the fork-PR entry point (no prior repo access).

evals.prompt: Run a CI security audit on the GitHub Actions workflows in evals/files/many-findings/ and walk me through which findings to fix.
evals.expected_output: ci-secure produces a report with nine distinct finding groups — the nine statically-detectable vectors (P14.7, P14.9, P14.10, P14.14, P14.15, P14.18, P14.19, P14.24, P14.25); the tenth, P14.11, is network-gated. At the finding-selection step the skill presents a full numbered free-text table of every group — never a capped 4-option widget — and dispatches one fix subagent per selected group.
expectations: All nine statically-detectable pattern groups render, each with its own attacker scenario.
Selection is a numbered free-text table, not AskUserQuestion.
Fix subagents are constrained to their single target file.
No commit/push/PR; the user reviews the working-tree diff.

evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/inject/ but assume gh is not installed.
evals.expected_output: The scan runs fully (the nine static vectors need no network). The impostor-SHA check (P14.11) is SKIPPED and both the terminal summary and the report say so loudly — a skipped network-gated check is never presented as a pass.
expectations: The output names the skipped impostor-SHA check explicitly.
The skill does not claim the repo is clean on the skipped check's behalf.
